plain_english: Which this world-born glory-natured, said to womb endless varied enjoyer-enjoyed — there whatever pervades as great-light-formed, that is like the great common, Supreme-Śiva-formed.
sanskrit_cite: yad idaṃ vibhavātmakaṃ bhuvanajātam uktaṃ garbhīkṛtānantavicitrabhoktṛbhogyaṃ tatra yad anugataṃ mahāprakāśarūpaṃ tat mahāsāmānyakalpaṃ paramaśivarūpam

plain_english: But whatever form pervading only some differences, that is a category — as earth called of glow-hardness-bulk-and-rest form, pervading all world-eggs ruled by world-lords from Kālāgni to Vīrabhadra.
sanskrit_cite: yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvaṃ yathā pṛthivī nāma dyutikāṭhinyasthaulyādirūpā kālāgniprabhṛtivīrabhadrāntabhuvaneśādhiṣṭhitasamastabrahmāṇḍānugatā

plain_english: There of these categories cause-effect-ness is shown; and it is twofold.
sanskrit_cite: tatra eṣāṃ tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo darśyate sa ca dvividhaḥ

plain_english: Ultimate, and of emission —
sanskrit_cite: pāramārthikaḥ sṛṣṭeś ca

plain_english: There the ultimate cause-effect-ness is this much: namely, of the agent-natured, free Lord, with such from-Śiva-to-earth-ended body, non-different in nature and resting in own nature — the showing-forth.
sanskrit_cite: tatra pāramārthika etāvān kāryakāraṇabhāvo yad uta kartṛsvabhāvasya svatantrasya bhagavata evaṃvidhena śivādidharāntena vapuṣā svarūpabhinnena svarūpaviśrāntena ca prathanam

plain_english: But the constructed cause-effect-ness, made by the Lord's will with necessity-breath: and as long as, when fixed before-after appearing, being even in the more, following own nature, only so far — by that from yogin's wish too, sprout from seed too, in dream and the rest, from pots and the rest, even thus.
sanskrit_cite: kalpitas tu kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ parameśecchayā niyatiprāṇayā nirmitaḥ sa ca yāvati yadā niyatapaurvāparyāvabhāsanaṃ saty api adhike svarūpānugatam etāvaty eva tena yogīcchāto 'pi aṅkuro bījād api svapnādau ghaṭāder apīti

plain_english: And there too, of the Supreme Lord non-loss of agency — thus even unconstructed, that ultimate stands firm.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi ca parameśvarasya kartṛtvānapāya iti akalpito 'pi asau pāramārthikaḥ sthita eva

plain_english: For with the ultimate wall-like standing form, all this drawn is fitting, not otherwise. Hence by the assemblage alone is caused-ness fitting.
sanskrit_cite: pāramārthike hi bhittisthānīye sthite rūpe sarvam idam ullikhyamānaṃ ghaṭate na anyathā ata eva sāmagryā eva kāruṇatvaṃ yuktam

plain_english: For it, made of the weave of all beings, by free-awareness greatness, thus of fixed own place-time-thing-mass nature — each thing-nature completed, being thus; of being-thus, being-otherwise — as it increases, so the effect's other-kind-ness by degrees nourishes.
sanskrit_cite: sā hi samastabhāvasaṃdarbhamayī svatantrasaṃvedanamahimnā tathā niyatanijanijadeśakālabhāvarāśisvabhāvā pratyekaṃ vastusvarūpaniṣpattisamaye tathābhūtā tathābhūtāyā hi anyathābhāvo yathā yathā adhikībhavati tathā tathā kāryasyāpi vijātīyatvaṃ tāratamyena puṣyati

plain_english: Thus the free-awareness-natured Supreme Lord alone, world-thing-bodied, is the maker of pots and the rest — since potter-awareness, from not being greater, and the potter's body placed amid the thing-mass — how is the potter-body's maker-pride? Thus — if Lord-made even that will be, like pots and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: ity evaṃ saṃvedanasvātantryasvabhāvaḥ parameśvara eva viśvabhāvaśarīro ghaṭāder nirmātā kumbhakārasaṃvidas tato 'nadhikatvāt kumbhakāraśarīrasya ca bhāvarāśimadhye nikṣepāt kathaṃ kumbhakāraśarīrasya kartṛtvābhimānaḥ iti cet parameśvarakṛta evāsau ghaṭādivat bhaviṣyati

plain_english: Hence the assemblage-doctrine too strengthens makership of awareness alone, the world-bodied.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt sāmagrīvādo 'pi viśvaśarīrasya saṃvedanasyaiva kartṛtāyām upodbalakaḥ

plain_english: For a pot such as would be there on Meru would not be.
sanskrit_cite: merau hi tatrasthe na bhavet tathāvidho ghaṭaḥ

plain_english: Thus in the constructed caused-ness, the many-typed-ness toward categories' cause-effect-ness in scriptures — that too fits — from dung, worms, from yogin's wish, from mantra, from herbs: like scorpion-arising.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kalpite 'smin kāryatve śāstreṣu tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ prati yat bahuprakāratvaṃ tad api saṃgataṃ gomayāt kīṭāt yogīcchāto mantrād auṣadhāt vṛścikodayavat

plain_english: There by own-system view we show the constructed.
sanskrit_cite: tatra nijatantradṛśā taṃ kalpitaṃ darśayāmaḥ

plain_english: There the Supreme Lord, full with five powers — thus said; he by freedom manifesting power after power chiefly stands fivefold.
sanskrit_cite: tatra parameśvaraḥ pañcabhiḥ śaktibhiḥ nirbhara ity uktam sa svātantryāt śaktiṃ tāṃ tāṃ mukhyatayā prakaṭayan pañcadhā tiṣṭhati

plain_english: Where awareness leads: Śiva-principle; where bliss leads: power-principle; where will leads: Sadāśiva-principle — for will, of knowing and doing, is of even-acceptance nature; where knowledge-power leads: Īśvara-principle; where action-power leads: knowledge-principle — thus.
sanskrit_cite: citprādhānye śivatattvam ānandaprādhānye śaktitattvam icchāprādhānye sadāśivatattvam icchāyā hi jñānakriyayoḥ sāmyarūpābhyupagamātmakatvāt jñānaśaktiprādhānye īśvaratattvam kriyāśaktiprādhānye vidyātattvam iti

plain_english: And here the category-lords: Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, Ananta — like Brahmā in withdrawal; of these common-formed, the particulars with pervasion for object are five — namely Śāmbhavas, Śāktas, Mantramāheśvaras, Mantreśvaras, Mantras — thus the pure path.
sanskrit_cite: atra ca tattveśvarāḥ śivaśaktisadāśiveśvarānantāḥ brahmeva nivṛttau eṣāṃ sāmānyarūpāṇāṃ viśeṣā anugativiṣayāḥ pañca tadyathā śāmbhavāḥ śāktāḥ mantramaheśvarāḥ mantreśvarāḥ mantrā iti śuddhādhvā

plain_english: So far directly Śiva is maker; but the impure path Aghoreśa, also called Ananta, emits — by the Lord's will-sway, for the enjoyment-perfection of atoms wavered by craving.
sanskrit_cite: iyati sākṣāt śivaḥ kartā aśuddhaṃ punar adhvānam anantāparanāmāghoreśaḥ sṛjati īśvarecchāvaśena prakṣubdhabhogalolikānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhyartham

plain_english: There the waverer, not-full, other-natured form, throbbing, actionless, mere longing — will be future fitness for bounding, thus: not impurity of man, nor another category.
sanskrit_cite: tatra loliko 'pūrṇam anyatārūpaḥ parispandaḥ akarmakam abhilāṣamātram eva bhaviṣyad avacchedayogyateti na malaḥ puṃsas tattvāntaram

plain_english: But passion-principle is longing bounded by action.
sanskrit_cite: rāgatattvaṃ tu karmāvacchinno 'bhilāṣaḥ

plain_english: But action there is mere action; mind-nature is passion, varied by action-difference — thus the distinction will be told.
sanskrit_cite: karma tu tatra karmamātraṃ buddhidharmas tu rāgaḥ karmabhedacitra iti vibhāgo vakṣyate

plain_english: It is this impurity from the Supreme Lord's self-veiling wish — nothing else at all a thing; and that too by that Lord-wish-nature alone is the thingness of earth and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: so 'yaṃ malaḥ parameśvarasya svātmapracchādanecchātaḥ nānyat kiṃcit vastv api ca tatparameśvarecchātmanaiva dharāder api vastutvāt

plain_english: And it, impurity, existing in the knowledge-kevalin, facing destruction — thus does not fatten its own effect, action.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca malo vijñānakevale vidyamāno dhvaṃsonmukha iti na svakāryaṃ karma āpyāyati

plain_english: But of the dissolution-kevalin, merely yawning it has been — thus impurity-strengthened action is the cause in transmigration-variety enjoyment — thus for the enjoyment-perfection of atoms pierced by enjoyment-latency of that, glorious Aghoreśa emits — thus it is said fittingly: and the stirring of impurity is by Lord-wish-force alone, for of the inert by itself, anywhere at all, is inability.
sanskrit_cite: pralayakevalasya tu jṛmbhamāṇa eva āsta iti malopodbalitaṃ karma saṃsāravaicitryabhoge nimittam iti tadbhogavāsanānuviddhānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhaye śrīmān aghoreśaḥ sṛjati iti yuktam uktaṃ malasya ca prakṣobha īśvarecchābalād eva jaḍasya svataḥ kutracid api asāmarthyāt

plain_english: An atom, indeed, is called mere shining of conscious-unconscious-form; of it conscious-form is lordliness alone, unconscious-formedness alone is impurity. And of it emitting, by Lord-wish-made, and thence always of the ever-to-be-emitted-thing-abiding form's to-be-shown-as-inert-ness, inert, all-effect-pervading-formed and pervasive is Māyā-called principle, the material cause; and showing it forth is the Supreme Lord's power named Māyā, quite other than that.
sanskrit_cite: aṇur nāma kila cidacidrūpāvabhāsa eva tasya cidrūpam aiśvaryam eva acidrūpataiva malaḥ tasya ca sṛjataḥ parameśvarecchāmayaṃ tata eva ca nityaṃ srakṣyamāṇavastugatasya rūpasya jaḍatayābhāsayiṣyamāṇatvāt jaḍaṃ sakalakāryavyāpanādirūpatvāc ca vyāpakaṃ māyākhyaṃ tattvam upādānakāraṇaṃ tadavabhāsakāriṇī ca parameśvarasya māyā nāma śaktis tato 'nyaiva

plain_english: Thus of kalā-and-rest principles to earth-ended too two-formedness is to be described.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kalāditattvānāṃ dharāntānām api dvairūpyaṃ nirūpyam

plain_english: And here proof too have said Abhinavagupta's gurus in two-formedness.
sanskrit_cite: atra ca dvairūpye pramāṇam api āhur abhinavaguptaguravaḥ

plain_english: Which in resolve shines, that separated too exists outside, with clear form — like a pot.
sanskrit_cite: yat saṃkalpe bhāti tat pṛthagbhūtaṃ bahir api asti sphuṭena vapuṣā ghaṭa iva

plain_english: And thus of Māyā-kalā-and-sky-flowers and the rest too this very course — thus the purely affirmative reason.
sanskrit_cite: tathā ca māyākalādikhapuṣpāder api eṣaiva vartanī iti kevalānvayī hetuḥ

plain_english: And by this, those who enjoy knowing of direct-realization-form with Māyā-kalā-nature-mind and the rest as object — they too are perfected, perfected alone.
sanskrit_cite: anena ca māyākalāprakṛtibuddhyādiviṣayaṃ sākṣātkārarūpaṃ jñānaṃ ye bhajante te 'pi siddhāḥ siddhā eva

plain_english: Thus standing, from Māyā-principle is world-birth.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ sthite māyātattvāt viśvaprasavaḥ

plain_english: And it though indeed non-sequential alone, yet by the stated view sequence appears — thus.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca yady api akramam eva tathāpi uktadṛśā kramo 'vabhāsate iti

plain_english: And that too is told: there per self the kalā-and-rest group is divided.
sanskrit_cite: so 'pi ucyate tatra pratyātma kalādivargo bhinnaḥ

plain_english: From its effect's makership-strengthening and the rest, by self-difference found — but that group sometimes might become one too, by the Lord's wish, like social selves — there all this kalā-and-rest group is pure, which by Lord-objectedness, fit for gaining its nature, doing own work, from world-opposition.
sanskrit_cite: tatkāryasya kartṛtvopodbalanādeḥ pratyātmabhedena upalambhāt sa tu vargaḥ kadācit ekībhavet api īśvarecchayā sāmājikātmanām iva tatra sarvo 'yaṃ kalādivargaḥ śuddhaḥ yaḥ parameśvaraviṣayatayā tatsvarūpalābhānuguṇanijakāryakārī saṃsārapratidvaṃdvitvāt

plain_english: And it becomes thus by the Supreme Lord's power-descent sway — thus we shall tell in its showing.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca parameśvaraśaktipātavaśāt tathā bhavati iti vakṣyāmas tatprakāśane

plain_english: But the impure is opposite of that.
sanskrit_cite: aśuddhas tu tadviparītaḥ

plain_english: There from Māyā kalā is born, which yokes the sleeping-placed atom with slight makership; and she, as if swelling, from the union of the two, Māyā and atom, though arisen deforms Māyā, not the undeformable atom — thus Māyā-effect-ness of her.
sanskrit_cite: tatra māyātaḥ kalā jātā yā suptasthānīyam aṇuṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvena yunakti sā ca ucchūnateva saṃsārabījasya māyāṇvor ubhayoḥ saṃyogāt utpannāpi māyāṃ vikaroti na avikāryam aṇum iti māyākāryatvam asyāḥ

plain_english: Thus from mutual clinging, indistinguishable inwardness of man-and-kalā.
sanskrit_cite: evam anyonyaśleṣāt alakṣaṇīyāntaratvaṃ puṃskalayoḥ

plain_english: Māyā-womb officers, but by some lord's grace, when all action ends, Māyā-man discrimination comes about — by which above Māyā sits the knowledge-kevalin; never ever below Māyā is kalā-man discrimination, by which one stands above kalā.
sanskrit_cite: māyāgarbhādhikāriṇas tu kasyacid īśvarasya prasādāt sarvakarmakṣaye māyāpuruṣaviveko bhavati yena māyordhve vijñānākala āste na jātucit māyādhaḥ kalāpuṃviveko vā yena kalordhve tiṣṭhati

plain_english: Or nature-man discrimination, by which below the chief one would not transmigrate.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtipuruṣaviveko vā yena pradhānādho na saṃsaret

plain_english: But in impurity-man discrimination: Śiva-likeness.
sanskrit_cite: malapuruṣaviveke tu śivasamānatvam

plain_english: But when man's fullness is seen, Śiva-ness alone.
sanskrit_cite: puruṣapūrṇatādṛṣṭau tu śivatvam eveti

plain_english: Thus kalā-principle alone is slight-makership-giving, not —
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kalātattvam eva kiṃcitkartṛtvadāyi na ca

plain_english: makership of the unknowing — thus.
sanskrit_cite: kartṛtvam ajñasya iti

plain_english: Slight-knowing-giving impure knowledge is born from kalā; and knowledge sees mind, and grasps its-lying parts and pleasures and the rest with discrimination.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃcijjñatvadāyiny aśuddhavidyā kalāto jātā sā ca vidyā buddhiṃ paśyati tadgatāṃś ca sukhādīn vivekena gṛhṇāti

plain_english: Of mind, of quality-confused form, with discrimination to grasp, from inability.
sanskrit_cite: buddher guṇasaṃkīrṇākārāyā vivekena grahītum asāmarthyāt

plain_english: Hence the mind-mirrored being is discerned by knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tasmāt buddhipratibimbito bhāvo vidyayā vivicyate

plain_english: Slight-makership, to perfect some part, somewhere alone makership — in this sense it comes down; but somewhere too in this part is passion-principle's business.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ kiṃcidbhāgasiddhaye kvacid eva kartṛtvam ity atra arthe paryavasyati kvacid eva ca ity atra bhāge rāgatattvasya vyāpāraḥ

plain_english: Not from non-dispassion-made is that — even of non-dispassion, seeing no-attachment.
sanskrit_cite: na ca avairāgyakṛtaṃ tat avairāgyasyāpi araktidarśanāt

plain_english: In dispassion, even in duty and the rest, attachment is seen.
sanskrit_cite: vairāgye dharmādāv api raktir dṛśyate

plain_english: Of the sated in food and the rest, though non-dispassion absent, from unremoved inner passion.
sanskrit_cite: tṛptasya ca annādau avairāgyābhāve 'pi antaḥstharāgānapāyāt

plain_english: By that, without again: from non-dispassion-non-arising contingency.
sanskrit_cite: tena vinā punar avairāgyānutpattiprasaṅgāt

plain_english: And time, effect reckoning, reckons makership too bounded by that — in the like, in some-where-ness, this alone makership — thus in this sense is necessity's business.
sanskrit_cite: kālaś ca kāryaṃ kalayaṃs tadavacchinnaṃ kartṛtvam api kalayati tulye kvacittve asminn eva kartṛtvam ity atrārthe niyater vyāpāraḥ

plain_english: In cause-effect-ness too hers alone is the business; by that from kalā alone this fourfold is born — this very, slightly now knowing, clinging, I-do — thus-formed awareness, gone to body-city-eight and the rest, is called beast.
sanskrit_cite: kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi asyā eva vyāpāraḥ tena kalāta eva etac catuṣkaṃ jātam idam eva kiṃcid adhunā jānan abhiṣvaktaḥ karomi ity evaṃrūpā saṃvid dehapuryaṣṭakādigatā paśur ity ucyate

plain_english: That this Māyā-and-rest six is called six sheaths.
sanskrit_cite: tad idaṃ māyādiṣaṭkaṃ kañcukaṣaṭkam ucyate

plain_english: Of awareness by Māyā, from being set aside, of kalā and the rest falling above, like sheaths from standing.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvido māyayā apahastitatvena kalādīnām uparipātināṃ kañcukavat avasthānāt

plain_english: Thus slight-makership which is Māyā-effect; there the slight, but, undistinguished which makership to be qualified; there engaged kalā is the cause of knowledge-and-rest birth — thus described.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ yat māyākāryaṃ tatra kiṃcit tv aviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ viśeṣyaṃ tatra vyāpriyamāṇā kalā vidyādiprasavahetuḥ iti nirūpitam

plain_english: Now the qualifier part which is called slight is to be known, and the effect — and as long as she, kalā, makes apart from own self, so long this very, of enjoyment-particular interwoven with pleasure-pain-delusion-nature, of mere common, of that-guṇa-sameness-alias, of nature-principle is the emission — thus of enjoyer-enjoyed pair together dependent on kalā-principle is emission.
sanskrit_cite: idānīṃ viśeṣaṇabhāgo yaḥ kiṃcid ity ukto jñeyaḥ kāryaś ca taṃ yāvat sā kalā svātmanaḥ pṛthak kurute tāvat eṣa eva sukhaduḥkhamohātmakabhogyaviśeṣānusyūtasya sāmānyamātrasya tadguṇasāmyāparanāmnaḥ prakṛtitattvasya sargaḥ iti bhoktṛbhogyayugalasya samam eva kalātattvāyattā sṛṣṭiḥ

plain_english: Here, and of these by the real path, emission is sequence-barren — thus said; sequence-appearing too is, and-is-thus, too said indeed.
sanskrit_cite: atra caiṣāṃ vāstavena pathā kramavandhyaiva sṛṣṭir ity uktaṃ kramāvabhāso 'pi cāstīty api uktam eva

plain_english: And sequence of knowledge-passion and the rest, though varied, is seen — someone loving knows, who knowing is loved, and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: kramaś ca vidyārāgādīnāṃ vicitro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ kaścid rajyan vetti ko 'pi vidan rajyate ityādi

plain_english: By that, describing differently, even in Raurava and other scriptures is uncontradicted to be deemed — but that very, become-stirred enjoyed-common: guṇa-principle.
sanskrit_cite: tena bhinnakramanirūpaṇam api rauravādiṣu śāstreṣu aviruddhaṃ mantavyaṃ tad eva tu bhogyasāmānyaṃ prakṣobhagataṃ guṇatattvam

plain_english: Where pleasure is enjoyed-form-light: lucidity; pain is light-unlight-swing-natured, hence very action-formed passion; delusion is unlight-formed darkness.
sanskrit_cite: yatra sukhaṃ bhogyarūpaprakāśaḥ sattvam duḥkhaṃ prakāśāprakāśāndolanātmakam ata eva kriyārūpaṃ rajaḥ mohaḥ prakāśābhāvarūpas tamaḥ

plain_english: The triad too, this enjoyed-formed.
sanskrit_cite: tritayam api etat bhogyarūpam

plain_english: Thus from stirred chief comes to-be-done-arising, not from unstirred — thus.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ kṣubdhāt pradhānāt kartavyāntarodayaḥ na akṣubdhād iti

plain_english: Stirring necessarily indeed in between to be assumed: thus proved Sāṃkhya-seen separated guṇa-principle.
sanskrit_cite: kṣobhaḥ avaśyam eva antarāle abhyupagantavya iti siddhaṃ sāṃkhyāparidṛṣṭaṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ guṇatattvam

plain_english: And that stirring from category-lord-presiding alone — otherwise toward fixed man, thus would not succeed.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca kṣobhaḥ prakṛtes tattveśādhiṣṭhānād eva anyathā niyataṃ puruṣaṃ prati iti na sidhyet

plain_english: Then from guṇa-principle mind-principle, where man-light and object offer reflection.
sanskrit_cite: tato guṇatattvāt buddhitattvaṃ yatra puṃprakāśo viṣayaś ca pratibimbam arpayataḥ

plain_english: From mind-principle I-maker, by which in mind-mirrored object-contact turbid, in man-light, in non-self is self-pride, like silver-pride in shell.
sanskrit_cite: buddhitattvāt ahaṃkāro yena buddhipratibimbite vedyasamparke kaluṣe puṃprakāśe anātmani ātmābhimānaḥ śuktau rajatābhimānavat

plain_english: Hence indeed making-ness by this is said of it; Sāṃkhya's but that does not fit — for he does not wish self's I-feeling-nature; but we wish makership too of it.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva kāra ity anena kṛtakatvam asya uktaṃ sāṃkhyasya tu tat na yujyate sa hi na ātmano 'haṃvimarśamayatām icchati vayaṃ tu kartṛtvam api tasya icchāmaḥ

plain_english: And that pure deliberation alone, non-rivalled, own-self-wonder-formed I — thus.
sanskrit_cite: tac ca śuddhaṃ vimarśa eva apratiyogi svātmacamatkārarūpo 'ham iti

plain_english: This is of it, of I-maker: instrument-heap.
sanskrit_cite: eṣo 'sya ahaṃkārasya karaṇaskandhaḥ

plain_english: But nature-heap of it alone is threefold, by lucidity-and-rest difference.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtiskandhas tu tasyaiva trividhaḥ sattvādibhedāt

plain_english: There the lucid, from which mind and the five mind-senses — and there in mind, in the generable, endowed with all-subtle-birth power, it is the begetter.
sanskrit_cite: tatra sāttviko yasmāt manaś ca buddhīndriyapañcakaṃ ca tatra manasi janye sarvatanmātrajananasāmarthyayuktaḥ sa janakaḥ

plain_english: In ear, distinguished by sound-birth power — thus; up to nose, fit with smell-birth fitness — thus elemental is not fitting: since I hear and the rest following, clearly I-maker-ness; and by instrument-ness necessarily maker-part-touching-ness; otherwise, if another instrument is joined, from regress-and-rest befalling.
sanskrit_cite: śrotre tu śabdajananasāmarthyaviśiṣṭa iti yāvat ghrāṇe gandhajananayogyatāyukta iti bhautikam api na yuktam ahaṃ śṛṇomi ityādyanugamāc ca sphuṭam āhaṃkārikatvam karaṇatvena ca avaśyaṃ kartraṃśasparśitvam anyathā karaṇāntarayojanāyām anavasthādyāpātāt

plain_english: And the maker-part is I-maker alone; by that two chief instruments: in knowing knowledge, in doing kalā — of the blind and of the lame; and from non-leaving of I-formed knowing-doing, from excelling in subtle-part, but from just the lucid I-maker, the five action-senses — I go, thus distinguished as I-maker, fit for effect-instrument; the foot-sense, its chief seat is outer, elsewhere too that is indeed — thus even of the crippled there is no going-break.
sanskrit_cite: kartraṃśaś ca ahaṃkāra eva tena mukhye karaṇe dve puṃsaḥ jñāne vidyā kriyāyāṃ kalā andhasya paṅgoś ca ahaṃtārūpajñānakriyānapagamāt udriktatanmātrabhāgaviśiṣṭāt tu sāttvikād eva ahaṃkārāt karmendriyapañcakam ahaṃ gacchāmi iti ahaṃkāraviśiṣṭaḥ kāryakaraṇakṣamaḥ pādendriyaṃ tasya mukhyādhiṣṭhānaṃ bāhyam anyatrāpi tad asty eva iti rugṇasyāpi na gativicchedaḥ

plain_english: And not from duty-confusion-freed alone, for the reason action is instrument-effected; and chief of goings and the rest is action-ness, not of form-and-rest grasping; of it, in Kaṇāda's system, since quality — hence necessarily to be admitted is the action-sense group.
sanskrit_cite: na ca kartavyasāṃkaryamuktād eva hetoḥ kriyā karaṇakāryā mukhyaṃ ca gamanādīnāṃ kriyātvaṃ na rūpādyupalambhasya tasya kāṇādatantre guṇatvāt tasmāt avaśyābhyupeyaḥ karmendriyavargaḥ

plain_english: And it, the pentad, from so-much-ness of joining.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca pañcakaḥ anusaṃdhes tāvattvāt

plain_english: Thus indeed: outside — first for giving up, or joining; for taking, or for both, or by both-less-ness for own-nature rest — there in order: anus, hand, foot, lap — thus.
sanskrit_cite: tathā hi bahis tāvat tyāgāya vā anusaṃdhiḥ ādānāya vā dvayāya vā ubhayarahitatvena svarūpaviśrāntaye vā tatra krameṇa pāyuḥ pāṇiḥ pāda upastha iti

plain_english: But within, in breath-seat-action joining, the speech-sense; by that, in sense-seat, in hand, whatever going, that too is foot-sense's alone doing — thus to be deemed; by that action-endlessness too does not bring sense-endlessness; to this extent of the rajasic clinging — thus they say.
sanskrit_cite: antaḥ prāṇāśrayakarmānusaṃdhes tu vāgindriyam tena indriyādhiṣṭhāne haste yat gamanaṃ tad api pādendriyasyaiva karma iti mantavyam tena karmānantyam api na indriyānantyam āvahet iyati rājasasya upaśleṣakatvam ity āhuḥ

plain_english: Others: from rajasic, mind — they say.
sanskrit_cite: anye tu rājasān mana ity āhuḥ

plain_english: Others: from lucid, mind; and from passionate, senses — thus.
sanskrit_cite: anye tu sāttvikāt mano rājasāc ca indriyāṇi iti

plain_english: But from enjoyer-part-coverer, from darkness-ruled I-maker, the subtle elements, knowable-one-formed, five.
sanskrit_cite: bhoktraṃśāc chādakāt tu tamaḥpradhānāhaṃkārāt tanmātrāṇi vedyaikarūpāṇi pañca

plain_english: Of sound-particulars, for stirring-natured, which one, unstirred-natured, pre-existent, common, undistinguished-natured — that is sound-subtle.
sanskrit_cite: śabdaviśeṣāṇāṃ hi kṣobhātmanāṃ yad ekam akṣobhātmakaṃ prāgbhāvi sāmānyam aviśeṣātmakaṃ tat śabdatanmātram

plain_english: Thus up to smell too is to be said.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ gandhānte 'pi vācyam

plain_english: There from stirred sound-subtle: space-giving-business ether; of sound, since bearing word-superimposition-room.
sanskrit_cite: tatra śabdatanmātrāt kṣubhitāt avakāśadānavyāpāraṃ nabhaḥ śabdasya vācyādhyāsāvakāśasahatvāt

plain_english: Sound-subtle stirred is wind; but sound of it is by ether from non-absence.
sanskrit_cite: śabdatanmātraṃ kṣubhitaṃ vāyuḥ śabdas tu asya nabhasā virahābhāvāt

plain_english: Form stirred is fire; the two earlier as before.
sanskrit_cite: rūpaṃ kṣubhitaṃ tejaḥ pūrvaguṇau tu pūrvavat

plain_english: Taste stirred is waters; the earlier three as before.
sanskrit_cite: rasaḥ kṣubhita āpaḥ pūrve trayaḥ pūrvavat

plain_english: Smell stirred is earth; the earlier four as before.
sanskrit_cite: gandhaḥ kṣubhito dharā pūrve catvāraḥ pūrvavat

plain_english: Others: by sound-touch, wind; in and-the-rest order, from five, ground — they think.
sanskrit_cite: anye śabdasparśābhyāṃ vāyuḥ ityādikrameṇa pañcabhyo dharaṇī iti manyante

plain_english: Mere heap of qualities is earth; no other quality-bearer at all.
sanskrit_cite: guṇasamudāyamātraṃ ca pṛthivī nānyo guṇī kaścit

plain_english: And in this category-cluster, the higher-higher-qualified is pervading; the lower-qualified, pervaded.
sanskrit_cite: asmiṃś ca tattvakalāpe ūrdhvordhvaguṇaṃ vyāpakaṃ nikṛṣṭaguṇaṃ tu vyāpyam

plain_english: It alone is the excellence of quality: that without it, another quality does not arise; by that, earth-principle, from Śiva-principle beginning, is pervaded by water-principle — thus water by fire, and the rest, up to power-principle.
sanskrit_cite: sa eva guṇasya utkarṣo yat tena vinā guṇāntaraṃ na upapadyate tena pṛthivītattvaṃ śivatattvāt prabhṛti jalatattvena vyāptam evaṃ jalaṃ tejasā ityādi yāvac chaktitattvam
